_doc: Anti-drift compass for the MARKETPLACE DEEPWALK EXPANSION arc (Ian 2026-07-24: 'expand and extend deepwalk journey with this same page, lay out the comprehensive roadmap'). Companion to MARKETPLACE_DEEPWALK_EXPANSION_ROADMAP.md. tools/marketplace_deepwalk_scoreboard.py reads this and emits MEASURED % per type / per phase / per MK class. EXPANSION means growing BOTH denominators: journeys x personas x states (board 1) and new MK dimension classes (board 2) - NOT re-verifying existing UFAI sub-layers (feedback_expand_dimensions_not_reverify).

_phases_def.G: ground - map the steps + surfaces + the code paths
_phases_def.W: walk - live-MCP deepwalk end-to-end carrying the FULL 99-dim lens (never spot-checks); requires >=2 personas AND >=2 states
_phases_def.H: harvest - Engine B night-crawl on a REAL observed friction, or mark clean
_phases_def.R: resolve - dim built / candidate killed / fix shipped / verified clean

_coverage_rule: A journey's W phase is 'done' only when walked in >=2 personas and >=2 states (including S-error or S-empty where reachable). One-persona/one-state = the shallowness this arc exists to kill.

MK9-response-sla-honesty.seed: Detail sheet renders 'Responds in ~1h - 95% reply rate - 1 sale'. Provenance unverified: computed from marketplace_inquiries, or seeded/static? | 2026-07-24 RESOLVED. DEFECT: response_rate/response_time_h were DECLARED in schema and DEFENDED by the trust guard (a seller may not self-assign them) but NOTHING EVER COMPUTED THEM - no trigger, function, edge fn or cron. So the buyer-facing 'Responds in ~1h / 95% reply rate' was a seeded promise about future behaviour that no real event could create, correct or invalidate. (The seller dashboard + public profile computed the same idea correctly from marketplace_inquiries, so only the buyer-facing column was orphaned.) FIX: mig 20260724000006 adds update_seller_response_stats() + a trigger on marketplace_inquiries (AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF replied_at,status), computing avg(replied_at-created_at) hours + replied/total, announcing itself via the seller_system_write GUC so the trust guard permits the SYSTEM write. Stays NULL until a first reply so a new seller is never shown a fabricated 0%. BACKFILLED: every seeded seller had ZERO inquiries, so all the fake 0.95/2.0h promises are now correctly NULL. TRIGGER PROVEN: 2 inquiries / 1 replied 3h later -> rate 0.50, time 3.0. LIVE: the detail sheet no longer claims any response SLA. KNOWN GAP: DELETE of an inquiry does not recompute (no delete path exists in the app; inquiries are closed, not deleted). | CONFIRMED ON REAL ACTIVITY via the J2 walk: a genuine buyer inquiry + a genuine seller reply drove the trigger to rate 1.00 / 0.0h with no manual intervention.
MK9-response-sla-honesty.distinct_from: MK1 governs trust BADGES/ratings; MK9 governs computed BEHAVIOURAL stats (a promise about future responsiveness).

MK10-ranking-sort-transparency.seed: The grid orders created_at desc with no disclosure of WHY these listings in this order. Ranking transparency is a legal duty for online marketplaces under EU P2B Art.5 and good practice everywhere. | 2026-07-24 FIXED: the grid ordered created_at DESC with NO disclosure, so a buyer could not tell recency from relevance from paid placement. The listings-info line now states it plainly: 'newest first. Sellers cannot pay for placement.' That is the EU P2B Art.5 ranking-parameter duty and, more importantly, an honest answer to 'why am I seeing these?'. VERIFIED live: 'Showing 9 listings - newest first. Sellers cannot pay for placement.'

MK10-ranking-sort-transparency.notes: | 2026-07-24 SWEEP: the grid on marketplace.html was disclosed earlier; the SECOND ranked list, the seller profile's own listing list, was not. It now carries the same VISIBLE line ('Newest first. Sellers cannot pay for placement.'), shown only when there is an order to describe. A title tooltip was written first and rejected: it never appears on touch, which is most of this audience (feedback_aria_label_only_is_invisible_to_sighted_users). The review list, capped at 20, now also says it is truncated, because the headline rating cites the canonical verified count and the two would otherwise disagree for a seller with more than 20 reviews. | 2026-07-24 HARVEST APPLIED (retrieve-first, no new crawl): substrate/external/external-deceptive-design-dark-pattern-taxonomy.md (deceptive.design/types). Audited the marketplace surfaces against its named patterns: FAKE SOCIAL PROOF was our real one and is what this turn fixed and gated (a rating with no reviews, Gold with no sales, Certified with no certifications). The rest came back clean, measured not assumed: 0 fake-urgency/fake-scarcity strings (no 'only N left', no countdowns, no 'N people viewing'), 0 preselected checkboxes or radios, fees disclosed three times ('no platform fees'), and COMPARISON PREVENTION is inverted here since we ship a compare mode. Hidden subscription / hidden costs are structurally impossible: there is no payment rail.

MK11-error-remedy-actionability.seed: An error must not propose a remedy the system knows cannot work. BORN FROM THE WALK (the roadmap's §8 rule that a harvest at spoke 5 refills the queue): this exact shape appeared FOUR independent times in one session - the buyer's inquiry step, platform-actions, founder-console and the saved-search save all answered an auth failure with 'Try again.' The write had failed because the SESSION was gone, so retrying reproduces it exactly; on the inquiry step the user had already typed a phone number before being told to repeat something that could never succeed.
MK11-error-remedy-actionability.notes: HARVEST: substrate/external/external-error-message-quality-guidelines.md (nngroup.com/articles/error-message-guidelines) - an error must give 'context and potential remedies' and 'instructions on how to resolve'; a remedy that cannot resolve it fails that on its own terms. DEFINE: a catch around a client WRITE that offers a retry must branch on the auth/permission case first. DETECT+SWEEP: tools/validate_error_remedy_actionable.py found 12 instances across 5 pages - a backlog the first ten classes never modelled, which is precisely why the denominator had to grow. FIX: centralized as window.whIsAuthFailure + whWriteError in utils.js. The split matters - the DETECTION is shared, but each site keeps its own tailored remedy ('re-save it', 'your message will go through', 'continue moderating'), because a specific instruction beats a generic one and flattening them would have cost exactly what the standard asks for. 4 catch(_) bindings had to be named before the error was even reachable. 12 -> 2, with every marketplace surface clear; the 2 left (analytics, dayplanner) are outside this arc and now held at a ratcheted floor. GATE: registered in run_platform_checks, 6/6 selftest, forward-only. The detector accepts EITHER the central helper or an inline signature test, because a first cut only recognised inline tests and went red on the very sites that had just been fixed properly - centralization must never read as a regression.

MK12-post-action-coherence.seed: A success message must not outrun the page. Saving a marketplace search toasted 'Search saved.' while the counter immediately beside it still read 0, and stayed 0 until a full reload: the handler reloaded the SHEET but never called updateSavedSearchBadge(), which already existed. Nothing was wrong with the write; the page disagreed with its own receipt, and a receipt contradicted by the number next to it teaches the user to trust neither.
MK12-post-action-coherence.notes: DEFINE: a handler that writes and then claims success must also re-derive the surfaces it invalidated. DETECT/SWEEP: tools/validate_post_action_coherence.py, 10 raw hits across 5 pages. FIX: the one REAL instance (saved-search badge) was fixed and verified live. Every other hit proved to be a FALSE POSITIVE, and each taught the detector something: the watchlist toggle refreshes OPTIMISTICALLY before the write (heart, then write, then confirm - better than refreshing after, and the first cut flagged exactly that correct shape); dayplanner/inventory/logbook emit DEGRADED or queued notices ('saved offline, will sync'), which are not commit receipts; and syncHeartIcons had to be recognised as a refresh verb, because the real file was passing only by accident on an unrelated updateCountBadges that happened to sit inside the scan window. All three are pinned as self-test cases. GATE: registered, 7/7 selftest, ratcheted at 0. The deliberate tolerance is the point - a gate that cries wolf on correct code gets ignored, which is worse than not having it.

MK13-reachable-capability.seed: An empty state must not promise what nothing can produce. Both admin consoles said 'No open disputes' for a queue no buyer can EVER file into - the dispute flow left with the payment rail.
MK13-reachable-capability.notes: DETECT: tools/validate_reachable_capability.py cross-references what each page LISTS against what the whole app can INSERT; a table read-and-listed but written by no page is unreachable from the UI. SWEEP found 4, of which 3 are legitimately server-fed (agentic_rag_traces via edge fn, equipment_reading_templates as a migration-seeded catalog, parts_staging_recommendations from the scheduled agent) and are allowlisted. THE FOURTH IS THE REAL ONE AND IT IS THE DEEPEST FINDING OF THE ARC: marketplace_reviews is SELECT-only on BOTH pages that touch it. There is no review-submission UI anywhere in the app, so no buyer can write a review - and because the verified-only rating is COMPUTED from reviews, a seller cannot currently earn a rating in-product at all. The MK1 work made the rating honest; this shows the ladder behind it has no first rung. Seeded data has reviews only because the seeder writes them with service-role. FIX is PARTIAL by design: the false promise is removed ('Reviews will appear here after buyers submit them' -> an honest statement that reviews are not open yet and what sellers ARE judged on), verified live on an unrated seller. Building the actual review-submission flow is a PRODUCT decision for Ian, not something to infer - it is the open fork this class surfaced. | 2026-07-24 FIX COMPLETED — Ian chose 'build the review flow', so the missing rung was BUILT rather than papered over. Migration 20260724000011 tightens mkt_reviews_insert to require STANDING (an existing inquiry from you on that listing, the only on-platform trace of a real interaction in a contact-only marketplace) and to forbid reviewing your own listing, while keeping the half that was already right: a buyer may only insert as themselves with verified_purchase=false. UI: a 'Write a review' control on the listing detail, shown only with standing, with pre-write validation and copy explaining that an unconfirmed review is shown but does not move the score. PROVEN LIVE end to end: no inquiry -> no control; after a real inquiry -> control appears; posting stored the review with verified_purchase=false; and Romeo then had 2 reviews (1 verified, 1 not) with rating_count still 1, i.e. the open form does NOT inflate the score. THREE FORGE ATTEMPTS RUN AGAINST RLS DIRECTLY, bypassing the UI gate, all blocked 42501: reviewing a listing never inquired about, self-claiming verified_purchase, and posting under another worker's name. The detector itself confirms the loop closed: marketplace_reviews dropped off its findings because a client insert path now exists. Probe rows removed; DB back to 15 seeded verified reviews and 0 inquiries.
